newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Nov 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Nov 7.

text.p: The following is a summary of major South Korean political stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not gaurantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.
- Diary uncovered from two killed North Korean guerrillas reveals that they even played electronic games at a ski resort while on the run from South Korean troops.
- President Kim Young-sam names top national security adviser Yoo Chong-ha to be foreign minister, replacing Gong Ro-myung who tendered his resignation in a surprise move.
- The venue of the 2002 World Cup fnal match is to be determined by lottery between Korea and Japan, FIFA said.
- Korean employers federation is subject of investigation on charges of illegal lobbying for tax favors and to secure advantage in dealing with trade unions.
- President Kim Young-sam named his chief foreign affairs and national security advisor, Yoo Chong-ha, as the new foreign minister.
- President Kim names foreign and security affairs secretary Yoo Chong-ha as foreign minister.
